simple.meaning: מְשׂוּרָה (mᵉsûwrâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a measure (for liquids).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Leviticus 19:35. The surrounding context includes family line, offering, righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְשׂוּרָה (H4884) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מְשׂוּרָה (mᵉsûwrâh) / H4884 is traced through Leviticus 19:35, 1 Chronicles 23:29, Ezekiel 4:11, Ezekiel 4:16 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “ ‘You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity.

timeline.evidenceText: “ ‘You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity.

for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
You shall drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin.† A hin is about 6.5 liters or 1.7 gallons. From time to time you shall drink.
Moreover he said to me, “Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight, and with fearfulness. They will drink water by measure, and in dismay;
